
NB the function ignores rounding of inputs when calculating max possible variance.

```{r}

library(tidyverse)

estimate_beta_distribution_from_mean_sd <- function(mean_val, sd_val, min_pos, max_pos) {
  # 1. Transform to proportionate scale (0-1)
  range_val <- max_pos - min_pos
  mu_prop   <- (mean_val - min_pos) / range_val
  var_prop  <- (sd_val / range_val)^2
  
  # 2. Constraint check: Variance must be < mu*(1-mu)
  # Using a small epsilon to avoid exactly zero or negative phi
  max_possible_var <- mu_prop * (1 - mu_prop)
  
  # 3. Calculate Beta shape parameters
  # phi is the 'precision' parameter
  phi <- (max_possible_var / pmax(var_prop, 1e-6)) - 1
  
  alpha <- mu_prop * phi
  beta  <- (1 - mu_prop) * phi
  
  # Handle cases where variance is too high for a Beta distribution
  invalid <- var_prop >= max_possible_var | alpha <= 0 | beta <= 0
  
  return(tibble(
    alpha = ifelse(invalid, NA_real_, alpha),
    beta = ifelse(invalid, NA_real_, beta)
  ))
}


```



```{r}

# 1. Define the parameters for your specific scale

# BDI-II-like data
# mean_val <- 25
# sd_val   <- 9
# min_pos  <- 0
# max_pos  <- 63

# # evaluations of 'love'
# mean_val <- 6.74
# sd_val   <- 0.54
# min_pos  <- 1
# max_pos  <- 7

# # "please respond with 7"
# mean_val <- 6.99
# sd_val   <- 0.14
# min_pos  <- 1
# max_pos  <- 7

# classic 3 evaluations of poop
mean_val <- 1.76
sd_val   <- 0.90
min_pos  <- 1
max_pos  <- 7

# 2. Get the alpha and beta estimates using your function
params <- estimate_beta_distribution_from_mean_sd(mean_val, sd_val, min_pos, max_pos)

```


```{r}

# 3. Generate the plot
if (!is.na(params$alpha)) {
  
  # Create a sequence of 1000 points between 0 and 1
  plot_data <- tibble(x_prop = seq(0, 1, length.out = 1000)) %>%
    mutate(
      # Calculate the density for each point
      density = dbeta(x_prop, params$alpha, params$beta),
      # Transform the x-axis back to the original scale for the plot
      x_original = x_prop * (max_pos - min_pos) + min_pos
    )
  
  # Create the ggplot
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = x_original, y = density)) +
    geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1) +
    geom_area(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
    theme_linedraw() +
    labs(
      title = "Estimated Beta Distribution",
      subtitle = paste0("Alpha: ", round(params$alpha, 2), 
                        " | Beta: ", round(params$beta, 2)),
      x = "Scale Value",
      y = "Density"
    ) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = mean_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    annotate("text", x = mean_val, y = 0, label = "Mean", 
             vjust = -1, color = "red", angle = 90, size = 3)
  
  dist_mean <- params$alpha / (params$alpha + params$beta)
  
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = x_prop, y = density)) +
    geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1) +
    geom_area(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
    theme_linedraw() +
    labs(
      title = "Estimated Beta Distribution",
      subtitle = paste0("Alpha: ", round(params$alpha, 2), 
                        " | Beta: ", round(params$beta, 2)),
      x = "POMP Scale Value",
      y = "Density"
    ) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = dist_mean, linetype = "dashed", color = "red")    

  } else {
  message("The provided Mean and SD are incompatible with a Beta distribution.")
}

```



```{r}

# 1. Calculate the bounds on the original scale
sd_lower <- mean_val - sd_val
sd_upper <- mean_val + sd_val
sd2_lower <- mean_val - sd_val*2
sd2_upper <- mean_val + sd_val*2

# 2. Update the plot
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = x_original, y = density)) +
  # Add the shaded SD region first (so it's in the background)
  annotate("rect", 
           xmin = sd2_lower, xmax = sd2_upper, 
           ymin = 0, ymax = Inf, 
           fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.5) +
  annotate("rect", 
           xmin = sd_lower, xmax = sd_upper, 
           ymin = 0, ymax = Inf, 
           fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1) +
  geom_area(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated Beta Distribution",
    subtitle = paste0("M = ", mean_val, ", SD = ", sd_val, 
                      " | Alpha: ", round(params$alpha, 2), 
                      " | Beta: ", round(params$beta, 2)),
    x = "Scale Value",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  # Reference line for the Mean
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  # Optional: Labels for the SD bounds
  annotate("text", x = sd_lower, y = 0, label = "-1 SD", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = sd_upper, y = 0, label = "+1 SD", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = sd2_lower, y = 0, label = "-2 SD", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = sd2_upper, y = 0, label = "+2 SD", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "grey50")
```

- Add POMP-SD/ROMP-SD estimates?

```{r}

# 1. Calculate the Proportionate (POMP) values
range_val <- max_pos - min_pos
mu_prop   <- (mean_val - min_pos) / range_val
sd_prop   <- sd_val / range_val
romp_sd <- range_val / sd_val

# 2. Define the SD bounds on the 0-1 scale
# We use pmin/pmax to ensure the shading stays within the logical 0-1 boundaries
pomp_sd_lower <- pmax(0, mu_prop - sd_prop)
pomp_sd_upper <- pmin(1, mu_prop + sd_prop)
pomp_sd2_lower <- pmax(0, mu_prop - sd_prop*2)
pomp_sd2_upper <- pmin(1, mu_prop + sd_prop*2)

# 3. Create the plot
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = x_prop, y = density)) +
  # Add shaded region for M +/- SD on the POMP scale
  annotate("rect", 
           xmin = pomp_sd2_lower, xmax = pomp_sd2_upper, 
           ymin = 0, ymax = Inf, 
           fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.6) +
  annotate("rect", 
           xmin = pomp_sd_lower, xmax = pomp_sd_upper, 
           ymin = 0, ymax = Inf, 
           fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1) +
  geom_area(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated Beta Distribution (POMP Scale)",
    subtitle = paste0("Prop. Mean = ", round(mu_prop, 2), 
                      " | POMP-SD = ", round(sd_prop, 2),
                      " | ROMP-SD = ", round(romp_sd, 2)),
    x = "POMP Value (0 to 1)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  # Vertical line at the Proportionate Mean
  geom_vline(xintercept = mu_prop, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  # Label the bounds
  annotate("text", x = pomp_sd_lower, y = 0, label = "-1 SD", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = pomp_sd_upper, y = 0, label = "+1 SD", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = pomp_sd2_lower, y = 0, label = "-2 SD", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = pomp_sd2_upper, y = 0, label = "+2 SD", 
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "grey50")
```
